clue.text: Grundy's holding top card, and gives comfort

indicators.note: holding has one piece gripping the other, so the top card sits inside Grundy's name

parts.note: Solomon Grundy of the nursery rhyme is shortened to Sol, and the possessive adds S
the ace is the highest card in many games

explanation.surface: Someone called Grundy, holding the best card, is generous with consolation.
explanation.walkthrough: Mrs Grundy, the prude, is the first Grundy that comes to mind; it is Solomon Grundy (born on a Monday), cut to SOL'S, that holds the ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To console someone is to give them comfort, and the verb in the third person matches.

clue.text: Old-clothes-man is strictly for the birds

definitions.text: Old-clothes-man is strictly for the birds

parts.words: Old-clothes-man is strictly for the birds
parts.note: a figure dressed in cast-off clothes, set up purely to deal with birds in a field; 'for the birds' also means worthless

explanation.surface: A dismissive verdict on a rag-and-bone dealer.
explanation.walkthrough: An old-clothes-man was a dealer in second-hand clothing; here he is a dummy wearing them, there only on account of the birds.
explanation.definitionFit: A dummy dressed in cast-off clothing stands in fields to frighten crows.

clue.text: Cats, doing the round of the track ?

definitions.meaning: cats drink milk by scooping it with the tongue

definitions.text: doing the round of the track
definitions.meaning: runners completing circuits of a racetrack

explanation.surface: Felines running a circuit of the racetrack.
explanation.definitionFit: Cats drink by lapping milk, and runners circling a track are completing laps.

clue.text: Barge-mistress

parts.note: the Egyptian queen whose barge 'like a burnish'd throne' is described in Shakespeare's Antony and ...

explanation.surface: A woman in charge of a canal boat.
explanation.walkthrough: A barge-mistress sounds like a canal boatwoman, but it is the queen in the golden barge on the Cydnus, and mistress of Antony as well.
explanation.definitionFit: Shakespeare's Egyptian queen sits in her gilded barge and is Mark Antony's lover.

clue.text: A hare sighted in W.1 ?

definitions.meaning: the old huntsman's cry raised when a hare is spotted
a district of central London within the W1 postcode

explanation.surface: Spotting a hare in the middle of London.
explanation.walkthrough: W1 is a London postal district; the district in it known for nightlife takes its name from the old hunting cry once heard in its fields.
explanation.definitionFit: The huntsman's hallo on sighting a hare named the central London district where hunts once ran.

clue.text: They make up and are defined by vital statistics

definitions.text: They make up and are defined by vital statistics

parts.words: They make up and are defined by vital statistics
parts.note: numbers are what any statistics are made of, and a woman's shape is described by the bust, waist and hip measurements called vital statistics

explanation.surface: A remark about numbers and bodily measurements.
explanation.walkthrough: The word works twice: numerals compose statistics, and bodily shapes are summed up by the three measurements called vital statistics.
explanation.definitionFit: Numerals compose statistics, and bodily shapes are what bust-waist-hip measurements describe.

clue.text: You might be rude, so look out, Dad !

parts.note: fore is the golfer's warning shout to look out
father is the formal word for dad

explanation.surface: A warning to Dad that someone may be rude to him.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition echoes Gray's Elegy, 'The rude forefathers of the hamlet sleep': your ancestor might well have been rude, meaning rough and unlettered; 'so' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An ancestor of yours, in Gray's Elegy, may be rude in the sense of uncultivated.

clue.text: Thanks be to God for beautiful girl !

definitions.meaning: a short prayer of thanks said before or after a meal
a girl's name that also means elegance and charm

explanation.surface: Giving thanks to heaven for a lovely young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: A prayer said at table thanks God, and the girl's name also means elegance.

clue.text: Eight overturned in the road put straight

indicators.note: in places the shuffled eight inside the abbreviation for road

parts.note: RD is the standard abbreviation for road

indicators.note: overturned means knocked over and disordered, so the letters of eight are rearranged

explanation.surface: Eight people knocked over in the street have been set upright again.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Eight overturned' suggests a capsized rowing crew, but 'overturned' is the anagram signal and 'in' places the result inside the road's abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: To set something right or correct it is to straighten it out.

clue.text: Begotten-by Sir Edward ?

parts.note: taken as written
Ed is the short form of the name Edward; the letters running across Sir Edward are this charade itself, a coincidence of spelling rather than a hidden word

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone was fathered by Sir Edward.
explanation.definitionFit: A child fathered by someone was sired by him.

clue.text: Some example is quite enough

indicators.note: some of a word means only part of it is used, so the letters sit inside the next word

explanation.surface: One instance is all that is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Plenty, more than sufficient, is a synonym of the clue phrase.

clue.text: Can Norwegian water cause very alcoholic rage ?

parts.note: hard liquor is strong spirits, so hard means very alcoholic
anger is a synonym of rage

explanation.surface: Asking whether drinking Norwegian water could make someone furious like strong spirits.
explanation.walkthrough: The Hardanger is a long fjord in western Norway; 'Can' and 'cause' are link words.
explanation.definitionFit: The Hardanger fjord is a famous stretch of sea water in western Norway.

clue.text: "This our life, — from public haunt" (A.Y.L.I.)

definitions.text: This our life, — from public haunt

parts.words: This our life, — from public haunt
parts.note: a line from the Duke Senior's speech in the Forest of Arden in Shakespeare's As You Like It, with one word left out

explanation.surface: A Shakespeare quotation with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: A.Y.L.I. is As You Like It; the full line is 'And this our life, exempt from public haunt, Finds tongues in trees'.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing word in the quotation means free from or excused, the forest life being away from crowds.

clue.text: Pretended to be emotionally involved

definitions.meaning: to put on a show of a feeling or manner, feigned

explanation.surface: Someone who faked being moved by something.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both feigned (affected an accent) and moved in feeling (deeply affected by the news).

clue.text: Weapon for use against the staff of life

definitions.text: Weapon for use against the staff of life

parts.words: Weapon for use against the staff of life
parts.note: bread is proverbially the staff of life, and the weapon is a serrated kitchen blade for slicing it

explanation.surface: An arm to wield in battle against a staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Staff' looks like a stick to fight against, but 'the staff of life' is a proverbial name for bread.
explanation.definitionFit: A serrated kitchen blade is the tool for cutting loaves.

clue.text: What fences do — with jewels perhaps

definitions.text: What fences do — with jewels perhaps

parts.words: What fences do — with jewels perhaps
parts.note: a fence is a receiver of stolen goods, and stolen gems are often given new mounts so they cannot be recognised

explanation.surface: What a receiver of stolen goods does with a haul of gems.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fences' look like garden barriers but are dealers in stolen property; such a dealer would put stolen gems in new settings, and reset is also an old Scots word for receiving stolen goods.
explanation.definitionFit: Placing gems in fresh mountings is to put them into a new setting again.

clue.text: The antithesis of Lucy's ways

parts.note: Wordsworth's Lucy poem begins 'She dwelt among the untrodden ways', so the opposite of un- gives ways walked again

explanation.surface: Contrasting a girl's habits with their opposite.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lucy's ways' suggests her habits, but they are the 'untrodden ways' of Wordsworth's poem; swapping the prefix for its opposite gives paths walked over again.
explanation.definitionFit: Paths walked over again and again are the opposite of paths never walked.

clue.text: Theatre performers make music on the hills

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece written on another sits above it, so the music comes before the hills

parts.note: opera is music drama
tors are rocky hills, as on Dartmoor in south-west England

explanation.surface: Stage actors singing in the hills.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Theatre' is the operating theatre, so the performers are surgeons; 'make' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Surgeons who perform operations in an operating theatre are operators.

clue.text: Like the patriarch with anti-snore proclivities

indicators.note: proclivities are leanings or tendencies, a hint that the letters of anti-snore are bent into another order

explanation.surface: A church leader who campaigns against snoring.
explanation.walkthrough: Nestorius was a 5th-century patriarch of Constantinople; 'with ... proclivities' asks for the letters of ANTI-SNORE to be rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective describes followers of Nestorius, patriarch of Constantinople, so like him.

clue.text: No nightcap this !

parts.note: a nightcap is worn in bed, while this soft broad-brimmed felt hat has a name meaning fully alert

explanation.surface: An exclamation that something is not bedtime headwear or a bedtime drink.
explanation.walkthrough: A nightcap is a cap worn in bed (or a bedtime drink); this felt hat, popular in the 19th century, is named for being far from asleep.
explanation.definitionFit: A low-crowned, broad-brimmed felt hat bears a name that also means fully alert.

clue.text: French nobleman and monarch take a dip

definitions.note: the definition is a verb phrase, the answer the matching -ing form as in 'go ducking'

parts.note: duc is French for duke
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: A French duke and a king go for a swim together.
explanation.definitionFit: Plunging briefly under water is a dip.

clue.text: Level money makes level

definitions.meaning: betting odds of one to one, where the winnings equal the stake
smooths or equalises, as one does a score

explanation.surface: A remark that money equalises things.
explanation.definitionFit: Even-money odds pay a sum equal to the stake, and to smooth something flat or equalise a score is to even it.

clue.text: "And with a stronger faith A sword, a horse, a shield " (Lovelace)

definitions.text: And with a stronger faith A sword, a horse, a shield

parts.words: And with a stronger faith A sword, a horse, a shield
parts.note: lines from Richard Lovelace's poem To Lucasta, Going to the Wars, with the rhyming verb left out

explanation.surface: A Cavalier poem's lines with a gap to fill.
explanation.walkthrough: The poet leaves Lucasta to take up arms instead, the 'new mistress' being the enemy and his sword.
explanation.definitionFit: The missing verb means to clasp or take up eagerly, as the poet does his weapons.

clue.text: Beethoven's highly graceful trio

parts.note: Arch- means chief or highly, and a duke is addressed as Your Grace

explanation.surface: Praise of an elegant piece of Beethoven chamber music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Highly graceful' reads as praise, but arch- is the prefix for chief and a duke is 'His Grace', so a chief Grace is a top-ranked royal prince of Austria.
explanation.definitionFit: Beethoven's Piano Trio Op 97 is named for its dedicatee, Archduke Rudolph of Austria.

clue.text: Advantage of a tip

parts.note: a vail is an old word for a gratuity given to a servant

explanation.surface: The benefit of a gratuity.
explanation.walkthrough: VAIL, an archaic word for a tip to a servant, is the piece most solvers will not know.
explanation.definitionFit: Benefit or use, as in 'to no avail', is advantage.

clue.text: Rorke's meaning is somewhat aimless

parts.note: The word also means the gist of something, and to move without aim

explanation.surface: A remark that someone named Rorke talks without much point.
explanation.walkthrough: Rorke's Drift, a ford in South Africa, was the scene of a famous 1879 defence; the gist of what someone says is their meaning, and wandering without purpose is aimless.
explanation.definitionFit: The word completes the battle's name, means gist, and means wandering without purpose.

clue.text: Wooden curtain

parts.note: the political barrier around Communist China was named after a woody Asian grass, by analogy with the Iron Curtain

explanation.surface: A screen made of timber.
explanation.walkthrough: The Iron Curtain divided Europe; the equivalent barrier round Communist China was named after the woody plant, which also makes blinds and screens.
explanation.definitionFit: The woody grass gives its name to China's Cold War barrier and to slatted blinds.

clue.text: Eleanora might be accustomed to it

indicators.note: might be suggests that the actress's surname could become another word if its letters are moved

parts.note: Eleonora Duse was a celebrated Italian actress

explanation.surface: An actress who has grown used to something.
explanation.walkthrough: The surname of the actress Duse, rearranged, gives the answer; 'to it' rounds off the phrase 'used to it'.
explanation.definitionFit: Being used to something means being accustomed to it.

clue.text: Are they displayed by performers of the can-can?

definitions.text: Are they displayed by performers of the can-can?

parts.words: Are they displayed by performers of the can-can?
parts.note: the dance's name is read as 'can, can', so the dancers show things they are able to do

explanation.surface: A question about what cancan dancers put on show.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests high kicks and petticoats, but 'can-can' is read as the verb can twice, so the dancers display what they are capable of.
explanation.definitionFit: Capacities or talents are the things a person can do.

clue.text: Yes, a good beast

parts.note: OK is an informal way of saying yes
pi, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for good

explanation.surface: Agreeing that an animal is a fine one.
explanation.definitionFit: The giraffe's forest relative from the Congo is a large animal.

clue.text: He gets what's left.

parts.note: what's left here means what is bequeathed in a will, not the leftovers

explanation.surface: Someone who always ends up with the remains.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What's left' looks like leftovers, but it is what is left in a will.
explanation.definitionFit: A person named in a will receives the property bequeathed to them.

clue.text: Make out an amendment to rescind

indicators.note: an amendment alters something, so the word rescind is altered into a new order

explanation.surface: Interpreting a legal change to revoke something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'amendment to' asks for the letters of RESCIND to be rearranged; 'an' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To make something out is to perceive or detect it.
